candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record documents that after drainage of the pleural effusion, repeat CT showed near-complete left lower-lobe infiltrates in the space previously occupied by the pleural fluid, consistent with re-expansion pulmonary edema (RPE). The malignant exudative pleural effusion is the pre-existing condition whose rapid decompression precipitated RPE; it is a related/antecedent finding rather than the requested final diagnostic object.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Malignant pleural effusion is a contributing antecedent finding documented in the case, not the final diagnosis of re-expansion pulmonary edema

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis (RPE) is a post-procedural complication of pleural fluid drainage; the clinical record supports this with radiographic evidence of infiltrates filling the space vacated by the effusion.
Troponin not elevated and T-wave inversions suggest right heart strain from PE rather than myocardial injury, reinforcing RPE as the distinct final diagnosis.
